classification: MULTI_FACTOR (BOUNDED_ARCHITECTURAL_LIMITATION for the window-vs-structural-boundary mismatch + LOCAL_IMPLEMENTATION_DEFECT for document-identity.ts's whitespace bug). Neither requires a full-document fuzzy scan or an unbounded search - both fixes are additive and bounded.
explicitlyRejectedFixes: Simply raising windowChars from 4000/8000 to a larger constant (e.g. 12000/16000): rejected per the mission's own explicit prohibition AND per live-reproduction evidence (05) proving this alone would not resolve doc-b's real PRELIMINARY STATEMENTS recital or doc-a's real execution-date whitespace bug.

Removing the window entirely / full-document fuzzy matching by default: rejected - this would reintroduce the exact false-positive risk (mid-document incidental mentions read as relationship evidence) the window was originally built to prevent, and violates the mission's explicit 'no full-document fuzzy match by default' constraint.

chosenDesign.principle: Replace the fixed-character-count boundary with a STRUCTURAL boundary derived from the document's own already-computed StructuralIndex, with the existing fixed-window constant retained ONLY as a defensive fallback for documents where no structural index is available (e.g. malformed input, or a document with zero ARTICLE/SECTION nodes) - never as the primary mechanism.
steps: 1. relationship-resolution.ts's package-graph resolution entry point is given access to each document's StructuralIndex (already computed upstream in the pipeline for every document - confirmed no new computation is required, only wiring the existing object through).

2. A new helper, resolvePreambleBoundary(structuralIndex, documentId), calls structuralIndex.searchStructuralNodes(predicate) to find the EARLIEST (lowest charStart) node of nodeType 'ARTICLE' or 'SECTION' for that document (compiler/types.ts:70's own existing nodeType union - no new node kind needed). That node's charStart becomes the document's structural preamble-boundary: everything before it is caption + recitals + signature-block-of-the-caption-page + defined-terms-are-not-yet-declared front matter, by construction (Article/Section numbering is where the substantive numbered body begins in every financing-document convention this codebase already parses).

3. findAllAgreementReferences and findRecitalBounds are called against `doc.text.slice(0, preambleBoundary)` instead of a fixed 4000/8000-char slice. When no ARTICLE/SECTION node exists for a document (structuralIndex.searchStructuralNodes returns empty), the code falls back to the EXISTING fixed windowChars logic unchanged - a defensive floor, not a magic-number-widening fix.

4. findRecitalBounds (relationship-resolution.ts:174-181) is extended to recognize a second recital-heading convention: 'PRELIMINARY STATEMENTS' (case-insensitive, \s+-tolerant across any internal whitespace), alongside the existing WHEREAS keyword - both are real, observed drafting conventions for the same structural concept (a recital block), not a Superior-specific special case; the mission's own governing docs and this session's live reproduction (05) are the evidence base, and the fix is named generically ('a second recognized recital-heading convention') rather than keyed to any document caption or package.

5. document-identity.ts:38's executionDate regex is fixed the same way Mission 2 fixed document-classifier.ts: literal spaces in `dated (?:as of )?` replaced with \s+-tolerant equivalents (`dated\s+(?:as\s+of\s+)?`), applying the identical, already-validated whitespace-tolerance principle (layout-whitespace tolerance, not text normalization - the regex still runs against raw, unnormalized text) to a second, independently-discovered occurrence of the same defect class.
chosenDesign.totalContextBudgetStaysBounded: The structural boundary is typically SMALLER than the existing fixed window for a normal document (most Article I numbering begins well under 4000 chars in) and grows only as large as the document's OWN real front matter actually is when that front matter is unusually long (Superior doc-b's case) - it is bounded by the document's own structure, not unbounded, and never triggers a full-document scan. The fallback path preserves the current fixed-window behavior exactly for any document lacking a structural index, so no existing passing case regresses.

explicitEvidenceProvenance: findAllAgreementReferences already returns match offsets/rawText per reference (existing behavior, unchanged); the structural-boundary fix only changes WHERE the scan looks, not what evidence format it returns - so downstream confidence/classification logic (classifyReferenceEvidence, resolveAgreementReference) is unaffected in its own decision logic and continues to require the SAME operative-tie/recital-tie evidence quality it already requires before upgrading a candidate past REVIEW_REQUIRED.

safetyPreserved.ambiguityStaysReviewRequired: No change to resolveAgreementReference's own confidence-gating logic (relationship-resolution.ts:441-454's own REVIEW_REQUIRED-on-recital-only-evidence rule is untouched) - widening WHERE evidence can be found does not change HOW STRONG evidence must be to auto-resolve. A recital-only match remains supporting-strength-only evidence requiring human confirmation, exactly as today.
safetyPreserved.noRelationshipManufacturedFromMereMentio: classifyReferenceEvidence's existing CONTEXTUAL_MENTION_ONLY/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE classification (relationship-resolution.ts:476ff, untouched) continues to apply identically regardless of whether a reference was found via the old fixed window or the new structural boundary - a mere mention outside an operative-tie or recital-tie context is still never promoted to relationship evidence.
safetyPreserved.existingSafetyBehaviorPreserved: Every existing passing package-graph/relationship-resolution test (confirmed in 00-baseline.json's test baseline) exercises documents whose real structural preamble-boundary is expected to fall within or near the current fixed window in the common case (short, single-agreement documents), so the fallback-preserving design change should not alter their outcome; this will be confirmed empirically by re-running the full existing suite unmodified after implementation (Section on implementation gates).

outOfScopeExplicitlyExcluded: No hardcoded Article I or Section 1.01 reference anywhere in the fix - the boundary is computed generically from whichever ARTICLE/SECTION node happens to occur earliest in any given document.
No hardcoded document caption or package-specific string anywhere in the fix.

No combination with Unit A's semantic-computation logic - this fix lives entirely in lib/contract-model/compiler/package-graph/ and lib/contract-model/compiler/package-graph/document-identity.ts, disjoint from lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/ and lib/contract-model/ir/ which Unit A touches.
conclusion: Proceed to implementation. This is a bounded, additive, generically-named structural-navigation fix plus one independent whitespace-tolerance companion fix, matching the mission's own preferred architecture (Section 11) and explicitly avoiding every named anti-pattern (arbitrary fixed-offset widening, full-document fuzzy match by default, package-specific logic).
